reasons_add: BURHAN (author): An adjective restricts an indefinite noun but clarifies a definite one, so the divine attributes here praise rather than identify God. Abu al-Tayyib's verse illustrates praise through names that add no new identifying knowledge.
BURHAN (author): Omitting both verb and subject makes God's name alone open the utterance, accords with intending to remember Him alone, and lets the formula serve before any action.
BURHAN (author): The omission lets the utterance open with God's name alone and expresses the intention to remember Him alone.
ITQAN (Prophet, report through Burayda): He promised to teach a verse given to no prophet after Solomon except himself, identifying the basmala.
ITQAN (Ibn ʿAbbas): People overlooked the basmala, a verse revealed to none before Muhammad except Solomon.
ITQAN reports Burayda's account of the Prophet's promise and Ibn ʿAbbas's warning that people overlooked this verse; both say only Solomon previously received it.

question: 1:1/q42
position: Someone unable to recite al-Fātiḥa must substitute seven other verses in prayer.
reasons: ITQAN (author): The reciter's inability to read al-Fātiḥa requires a substitute of seven verses.

reasons_add: ITQAN (Ibn Masʿūd): The revealed basmala disclosed where one sura ended and another began. ITQAN (Abū Shāma): Gabriel may have signaled the end during the Prophet's review, or the basmala may have descended after all a sura's verses.
ITQAN (Abū Shāma): The Prophet's use of the word nuzūl for the basmala supports its Qurʾānic status.
ITQAN (Ibn ʿAbbās): A sound report transmitted by Ibn Khuzayma and al-Bayhaqī identifies al-Fātiḥa as the seven oft-repeated verses and counts the basmala as its seventh.
ITQAN (Ibn ʿAbbās): Ibn Khuzayma and al-Bayhaqī transmit the identification with a sound chain.
ITQAN (ʿAlī): In a sound report, al-Ḥamdu li-llāh is six verses and the basmala supplies the seventh.
ITQAN (ʿAlī): A sound report counts six verses from al-Ḥamdu li-llāh and one basmala verse.
ITQAN (Prophet, through Ibn ʿUmar): This report about Gabriel first conveying the basmala with revelation is graded weak.
ITQAN (Ibn ʿUmar): A separate transmission through Nāfiʿ says the basmala was revealed in every sura.
ITQAN (Ibn ʿUmar): A distinct report says he recited the basmala in prayer and after each sura, explaining that its inscription in the muṣḥaf calls for recitation.
ITQAN (Prophet, through Abū Hurayra): A sound report commands reciting the basmala with al-Ḥamd because it is one of al-Fātiḥa's verses.
ITQAN (Prophet, through Abū Hurayra): A sound report commands recitation of the basmala with al-Ḥamd.

question: 1:1/q41
position: Mentioning God and His attributes leads the worshipper into direct address, humility, and a plea for His help.
reasons: ITQAN (author): Al-Fātiḥa moves from God's names and attributes to addressing the Master of Judgment Day, prompting humility and the request for help.

reasons_add: ITQAN (Ubayy b. Kaʿb): His report says neither Torah nor Gospel contains a counterpart to the Mother of the Qurʾān, identified as the seven oft-repeated verses.
ITQAN (Ubayy b. Kaʿb): His report expressly identifies the incomparable Mother of the Qurʾān as the seven oft-repeated.
ITQAN (Ibn ʿAbbās): A report says the Opening of the Book equals two-thirds of the Qurʾān.
ITQAN (Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī): A man recited the Opening over a stung chief, who recovered; the Prophet asked how he knew it was an incantation.

ITQAN (ʿAbd Allāh b. Jābir): It cures every illness. ITQAN (Jābir b. ʿAbd Allāh): It cures everything except death. ITQAN (Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī): It cures poison. ITQAN (al-Sāʾib b. Yazīd): The Prophet treated him by reciting it with a light spittle-blow.
ITQAN (Anas): Reciting al-Fātiḥa and Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad at bedtime protects from everything except death.

question: What special virtues and healing effects are reported for al-Fātiḥa?

positions.position: It has no counterpart in the Torah or Gospel.
positions.reasons: ITQAN (Ubayy b. Kaʿb): His report identifies the unmatched Mother of the Qurʾān as the seven oft-repeated verses.

positions.position: It equals two-thirds of the Qurʾān.
positions.reasons: ITQAN (Ibn ʿAbbās): A report assigns the Opening of the Book this equivalence.

positions.position: Its recitation heals illness, poison, and stings; the Prophet also used it in treatment.
positions.reasons: ITQAN reports from ʿAbd Allāh b. Jābir and Jābir b. ʿAbd Allāh describe cure for every illness or everything except death; Abū Saʿīd reports cure for poison and a stung chief healed by recitation; al-Sāʾib says the Prophet recited it with a light spittle-blow to treat him.

positions.position: Reciting it with Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ at bedtime protects from everything except death.
positions.reasons: ITQAN (Anas): He reports this protection for the paired bedtime recitation.
